page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n4 family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is provisioned with 16 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It has a dedicated CPU allocation and a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this server type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the CPU performance of this instance in the average tier. The stress-ng single-core score is 1672.09, while the multi-core score is 7217.53. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1877.0 and a multi-core score of 7215.0. The Intel processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in specialized workloads. However, memory subsystem performance is a notable bottleneck; the PassMark memory score of 1718.22 falls into the bottom 25% tier, though cached small-block read bandwidth reaches 568.81 GB/sec. Large-block read and write speeds are lower at 68.85 GB/sec and 40.33 GB/sec, respectively.

This server is configured for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It achieves average performance in software compilation with a Geekbench clang score of 8701.0 and static web serving at 11.89 GB/sec. For machine learning, the hardware supports AMX, enabling prompt processing of 52.37 tokens/sec on a 7B LLM, though text generation on the same model drops to a weak 7.92 tokens/sec. The qualitative cost profile reflects a compute-optimized design where users pay for dedicated CPU resources while accepting a lower RAM-to-vCPU ratio and weaker memory performance. Appropriate workloads include CPU-bound tasks, software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight vector calculations.
